about.headline: WHO ARE THE REBELS
copy: Lane Kiffin took over at Ole Miss in 2020 and won {rec|55 games in six seasons}, and he didn't just win, he built an offense around receivers split way out wide, tempo, and a quarterback who could hurt you with his legs and his arm.

In 2025 it all came together around a quarterback nobody saw coming, as Trinidad Chambliss came over from Division II Ferris State, took the job in week three and threw for {yds|3,937 yards} with 22 touchdowns against three picks, ran for 527 more, and Kewan Lacy ran for 1,567 and a school record 24 touchdowns behind him as the Rebels went 11-1.

Kiffin left for LSU before the playoff, and Chambliss took them all the way to the semifinal and a 13-2 finish, and now he is back for one more year, and that is the offense we are building out of the Auburn playbook in College Football 27.

principles.title: SUPER WIDE SPLITS
principles.blurb: Force the defenders to spread out so much that there is too much room in the middle of the field to cover.
principles.detail: The receivers line up way outside, and every defender who walks out to cover them is one fewer in the box and in the middle of the field. With these wide sets, four verticals just works, because the safeties have so much room to cover.

principles.title: OPTION ROUTES
principles.blurb: The receiver reads the coverage after the snap: a curl or a sit against zone, a dig or a post against two high and match.
principles.detail: The option routes are what make it a veer and shoot. The slot reads it after the snap: up the seam or a curl against single high, a bender or a dig against two high and match. One call has an answer for all of it.

principles.title: THE QUARTERBACK IS A WEAPON
principles.blurb: Use the quarterback's running ability, arm strength and playmaking to add explosive plays on top of the base offense.
principles.detail: The base offense moves the chains against anybody. On top of it, the quarterback's legs and arm add the explosive plays: the QB power behind the bubble, the QB G Down out of empty, the seam shots down the field.

stats.note: Then a run to the playoff semifinal, and 13-2 at the end.
stats.label: REGULAR SEASON · 2025

stats.note: The third most in a season in Ole Miss history.
stats.label: CHAMBLISS · PASSING YARDS

stats.note: Plus 527 rushing yards and 8 more touchdowns on the ground.
stats.label: TOUCHDOWNS TO PICKS

player.name: TRINIDAD CHAMBLISS
player.line: From Division II to the playoff semifinal, and back for one more year.
player.bio: Won two Division II national titles at Ferris State, then transferred to Ole Miss for 2025 and took over the offense early in the season. He threw for {yds|3,937 yards}, the third most in a season in Ole Miss history, with 22 touchdowns against three interceptions, and ran for 527 yards and 8 more scores. He was the SEC Newcomer of the Year and won the Conerly Trophy, and the Rebels went 11-1 in the regular season and on to the playoff semifinal.
goodAt: Legs that turn the RPOs into a numbers problem.
Arm strength for the seam shots.
roleFor: The quarterback in this offense reads one defender on every RPO. The overhang over the slot or the defender over the bubble: if he stays home, the ball is handed off or kept, and if he bites down, the throw is behind him.
On top of the base offense he is the weapon. The QB power behind the bubble, QB G Down out of empty, the counter, and the arm to throw the skinny seam inside the safety.

lineage.name: TRINIDAD CHAMBLISS
lineage.brought: The legs and the arm both. The QB power behind the bubble, the runs out of empty, and the deep ball down the seams.

He is a receiver too: the swing with three blockers out in front of him, and the option route checkdown that sits down against zone and breaks away against man.

formations.name: Wide Trips
formations.desc: Three receivers to the wide side and one alone on the short side, all of them split way out. The RPOs, the swing, the verticals and the choice routes all live here, and the defense has to decide how many to put over the trips before every snap.
bullets: Count the defenders over the trips
Two high and a light box is a run
Single high and the seam is open

show.what: RPO Alert Bubble. Count them over the trips: two defenders over three receivers is a numbers advantage. The overhang bites on the run, the bubble goes out with two blockers in front.
RPO Alert Slot Slant. Both safeties back means five in the box against our five blockers and the back. The overhang stays home, so hand it off and get downhill.
Four Verticals. The splits spread the defense so far that the middle safety cannot get over to the trips side seam. Throw it as soon as he clears the flat defender.

formations.name: Empty Trips Y Off
formations.desc: Empty, with trips to the wide side and the tight end off the line on the other. Nobody expects a run out of it, so the quarterback runs are hitting a defense that lined up to stop the pass, and the man beater lives here too.
bullets: Nobody expects the run out of empty
The bubble with the quarterback power behind it
The motion in post against man

show.what: QB G Down. The trips pull the defense away from the run, the tackle blocks down, the guard pulls around for the edge and the quarterback follows him: five on four.
RPO Alert Bubble QB Power. They stay out there and take the bubble away, so the quarterback keeps it and follows the pulling guard to the second level.
Ins Slot Corner. Motion the solo receiver in. The corner is in outside shade with no safety in the middle, and the post leaves him all that ground to cover.

formations.img: art/Ole Miss__Empty Trips Y Off Formation.svg

formations.name: Spread
formations.desc: Three spread sets in one: Spread Wing Y-Flex with the jet motion, Wide Offset and Wide. Two receivers to each side, and the motion and the play action do the work: the jet series, the counter, the smash and the shots off the fake.
bullets: The play action holds the linebackers
Wide Offset and Wide for the deep shots

show.label: The jet series
show.what: Jet Touch Pass, Jet Power Read and Fake Jet FB Wheel all start with the same jet motion. Run the touch pass first, the user starts chasing the motion, and the other two open up.
PA Double Switch. The fake holds the linebackers, the streak we motioned across pulls the safety back, and the post comes in behind it.
PA Deep Choice. The switch release against match: the slot fade wheel and the post get vertical on the same plane, too much for the safety to get over in time.

pillars.name: Base Offense
pillars.line: The calls you can use against anyone at basically any time of the game. This is the backbone of the offense: run the ball or the RPO first to get a gauge on the defense, take what is there, and have a man beater ready, because people call man every single down. Everything else gets built on top of this.

Single high and the seam is open on four verticals
They call man and Ins Slot Corner makes them pay

pillars.name: Veer N Shoot
pillars.line: The two things that make the veer and shoot unique: the super wide splits and the option routes. This section is about letting the receivers read the coverage after the snap, and using the room the splits create to beat zone, man and match.

checks: The swing goes with no pre-snap tell and three blockers in front
Match coverage and the wheel is open on PA Deep Choice
The option route sits against zone and digs against match

pillars.line: The rest of the offense out of the same three formations, exclusive to Scheme Kings with a breakdown on every one: the quarterback runs out of empty and off the counter, the dagger, the jet series, the play action shots, the smash and the second man beater.

answers.name: Levels Seam
answers.label: The Skinny Seam Against Cover 3
answers.why: An excellent deep shot, and the key is the inside route on the trips side, a really skinny seam ball. Single high safety pre-snap, think Cover 3. He stems inside of the safety and ends up about the opposite hash. Hold it until he clears the safety or gets even with him, then pass lead it up inside the hash.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Middle player on the trips side on a streak.

answers.name: Four Verticals
answers.label: The Seam Against Single High
answers.why: These wide splits force the defense to spread out so much that the middle safety cannot get over to the trips side seam. Read the flat defender: if he jams and lets him go, throw it as soon as he clears. The middle safety does not have time to drive on it.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Inside slot on the trips side on a deep cross (the hot route), so he gets deeper down the field. Running back on an option route instead of his check and release hook.

answers.name: PA Deep Choice
answers.label: The Short Side Post
answers.why: If the switch release happens earlier, the post from the short side can get open against match. Against Cover 3 the option route pulls the middle safety back, the slot fade pulls the corner out, and the post is wide open for twenty five yards.
answers.do: Running back to the wide side of the field. Motion the outside receiver on the wide side (the option route) in. The slot who becomes the outside receiver on the wide side on a comeback. Outside receiver on the short side on a post. Running back on an option route, or leave him on the play action block for time.

answers.name: Four Verticals
answers.label: The Bender Against Two High
answers.why: The slot is on an option route. Against two high he does not keep going up the seam into the safety, he bends it into the middle and splits the two of them. If they have no true deep middle dropper, fire it in over the hook.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Inside slot on the trips side on a deep cross (the hot route), so he gets deeper down the field. Running back on an option route instead of his check and release hook.

answers.name: Double Smash Seam
answers.label: Against Cover 2
answers.why: If the user is using the mid read and stays too shallow, or there is no middle read on the field, the back splits the safeties.
answers.do: Running back to the wide side of the field. Outside receiver on the wide side on a streak. Outside receiver on the short side on a drag.

answers.name: Levels Seam
answers.label: Against Cover 2 With No Mid Read
answers.why: It works against Cover 2 too, but only when there is no middle defender: a Cover 2 sink, a Cover 2 blitz, or the user leaving the mid read. Split the two safeties with it.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Middle player on the trips side on a streak.

answers.name: Ins Slot Corner
answers.label: The Corner Route
answers.why: Maybe even better. A hard cut inside, then he breaks to the outside. Sometimes he breaks the defender off by five, six, seven yards. When the defender is in a trail position, touch pass it and let him run under it.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Motion the solo receiver on the short side in, about four or five yards, beside the tight end, and put him on a post. Inside slot on the trips side on a shallow cross.

answers.name: Switch Slot Cross
answers.label: The Corner Route
answers.why: One of our two best man beaters, with Ins Slot Corner. Look to the corner route first. Good separation as he breaks, let it fly.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field. Wheel route on the wide side on a corner route. Optional: block the running back if you think they are bringing pressure.

answers.name: Dagger
answers.label: The Drag
answers.why: The drag and the cross become a high low on the linebackers. Against man, the tight end drag runs away from his man.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Outside receiver on the wide side on a post sit.

answers.name: PA Deep Choice
answers.label: The Wheel Against Match
answers.why: The go to match beater in this scheme, against Quarters and Palms. The key is the switch release, the slot fade wheel with the post. The safety and the corner read one and two, and because both get vertical on the same plane, it is almost an impossible read for the safety to get over in time. Bomb it over the top.
answers.do: Running back to the wide side of the field. Motion the outside receiver on the wide side (the option route) in. The slot who becomes the outside receiver on the wide side on a comeback. Outside receiver on the short side on a post. Running back on an option route, or leave him on the play action block for time.

answers.name: Double Smash Seam
answers.label: The Back Against Match
answers.why: A concept built to beat match coverage. The vertical routes pull every match defender outside the hash, and the back gets a one on one with the linebacker up the middle. With a fast back on a linebacker, hit him over the top.
answers.do: Running back to the wide side of the field. Outside receiver on the wide side on a streak. Outside receiver on the short side on a drag.

answers.name: Deep Choice
answers.label: The Dig Against Match
answers.why: This is match coverage, with the safety playing at depth, and it is really hard for him to drive on this option route. As he cuts across the field he is going to option into the dig. Third and 20, we throw that for 22 yards.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Outside receiver on the wide side on a post. Outside receiver on the short side on a streak. Running back on an option route.

home.pitch: Super wide splits, option routes and a quarterback who runs it: RPOs with a throw built in, two man beaters you can trust, and shots down the field off the jet motion. All of it out of the Auburn playbook.

book.note: every formation and every call on the sheet lives inside it

plays.name: RPO Alert Slot Slant

reads.label: Read the Overhang
reads.text: Trips to the wide side, and the key defender is the one over the top of our slot, the middle player on the trips side running the skinny post. Keep your eyes on him at the snap.

reads.label: Count the Box
reads.text: Both safeties back means they are out of the box. Five blockers against four or five in there, and with the back that is a six on five numbers advantage for the run.

reads.label: Hand It Off
reads.text: If he stops his feet, steps outside or stays back over the slot, hand the ball off and get downhill. Double team, a reach block, nobody in the middle of the field, and it goes for a big pickup.

reads.label: The Skinny Post
reads.text: If he bites down, jumps down, comes downhill on the run, anything like that, throw the skinny post in behind him. Two safeties back opens up a great hole for it. On the goal line, read the most inside defender: he bites, drop it over his head.

reads.label: The Backside Slant
reads.text: An adjustment, and a third option. Put the solo receiver on the backside on a slant. They are overloading the trips side, so read the weak side linebackers the same way, and if they bite down, throw the slant.

reads.label: Nobody Over Number Two
reads.text: If there is nobody lined up over the number two receiver, put him on a post and stem it all the way up the field. He is basically uncovered, the inside defender stays inside, quick throw it.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Optional: backside solo receiver on a slant
plays.whenToUse: A great early down call, and the play to open against a new opponent: run the ball or the RPO first and get a gauge on what coverage he is in. Read the overhang over the slot. He stays home, hand it off. He bites down, the skinny post is behind him.

plays.name: Four Verticals

reads.label: The Seam Against Single High
reads.text: These wide splits force the defense to spread out so much that the middle safety cannot get over to the trips side seam. Read the flat defender: if he jams and lets him go, throw it as soon as he clears. The middle safety does not have time to drive on it.

reads.label: The Bender Against Two High
reads.text: The slot is on an option route. Against two high he does not keep going up the seam into the safety, he bends it into the middle and splits the two of them. If they have no true deep middle dropper, fire it in over the hook.

reads.label: One on One Against Match
reads.text: If they switch to Cover 3 match, match or man and the overhang turns and runs with the slot, the option route is now a one on one shot down the field. If you have a speed advantage, take it.

reads.label: The Deep Cross
reads.text: The other big time route. If the safety and the corners are playing too far over, or the user leaves the middle of the field to take the seam away, come inside to the deep crosser as he gets up over the linebackers. It works against man and match too.

reads.label: The Option Checkdown
reads.text: The back on his option route sits down against zone and breaks inside or outside against man. If every vertical is taken away, check it down to him.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Inside slot on the trips side on a deep cross (the hot route), so he gets deeper down the field
Running back on an option route instead of his check and release hook
plays.whenToUse: Four verticals is one of the most famous concepts in all of football, and out of these wide sets it is even better, because of how spread the field is. Single high, the seam. Two high, the bender. The deep cross and the option route underneath.

plays.name: Jet Power Read

reads.label: Read the Edge
reads.text: A power read is a read option, but inverted. Read the defenders on the edge as the jet motion comes across.

reads.label: They Shoot Upfield: Keep It
reads.text: If they shoot up the field because of the jet, keep the ball. The guard pulls across, follow him right through the hole, put your foot in the ground and explode up the field.

reads.label: They Stay Inside: Give It
reads.text: If they jump down inside, it is opposite: give it to the jet motion player as he comes across the field and get the edge. The tight end and the receivers pin everybody inside.

reads.label: Cut It Back
reads.text: If they take the edge away, cut it back. They overplay it, make a guy miss and turn it into a fifteen yard gain.

plays.whenToUse: A really good way to get the quarterback involved while attacking the perimeter with the jet motion. Jet Touch Pass and Fake Jet FB Wheel come off the same motion, so all three play off each other.

plays.name: Ins Slot Corner

reads.label: The Motion Post
reads.text: Motion the solo receiver in and most of the time the corner is in outside shade. Now when he goes up the field and breaks in on the post, it is so much ground for the corner to cover. No safety help in the middle of the field, take the one on one shot every time. A deep safety, throw it right away in front of him, do not lob it.

reads.label: The Corner Route
reads.text: Maybe even better. A hard cut inside, then he breaks to the outside. Sometimes he breaks the defender off by five, six, seven yards. When the defender is in a trail position, touch pass it and let him run under it.

reads.label: The Shallow Cross
reads.text: Two breakers underneath. The shallow cross is one on one with the linebacker or the safety. Throw it as it breaks inside.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: If everything else is covered, come all the way back to the drag from the outside receiver and fire it in over the middle of the field.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Motion the solo receiver on the short side in, about four or five yards, beside the tight end, and put him on a post
Inside slot on the trips side on a shallow cross
plays.whenToUse: The go to man beater in this offense. The motion in post wins against outside shade, the corner route breaks guys off, and the shallow cross and the drag are the answers underneath when the deep routes are covered.

plays.name: RPO Alert Bubble QB Power

reads.label: Eyes on the Bubble
reads.text: Trips to the wide side, and at the snap your eyes are on the bubble. Linebackers way inside and only two out there over the three, that is a three on two numbers advantage. Flip it out right away.

reads.label: Even Numbers: Snap It and Read
reads.text: If somebody is over the top of the three side, now we are even. Snap it, and if they bite down inside at the snap, we have the numbers again and throw the bubble.

reads.label: The QB Power
reads.text: If they stay out there and take the bubble away, keep it. The guard pulls across, follow him tight and get to the second level. It is an RPO, so half their defenders are playing the pass and you only have to worry about the box. Fifteen yards.

reads.label: The Bubble on the Crash
reads.text: If the defenders over the bubble crash at the snap, the one on one block outside gets even easier. Throw it, block the safety up ahead, twenty yards.

reads.label: The Short Side Hitch
reads.text: The third option. The bubble is taken away, the QB power is taken away by the user blitzing through the hole, so get it out to the hitch on the short side for a few yards.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The quarterback run with a bubble screen built in. Count the bubble side: three on two, flip it out. If they take the bubble away, the QB power is behind the pulling guard. Do not call it against a zero man blitz.

plays.name: Levels Seam

reads.label: The Skinny Seam Against Cover 3
reads.text: An excellent deep shot, and the key is the inside route on the trips side, a really skinny seam ball. Single high safety pre-snap, think Cover 3. He stems inside of the safety and ends up about the opposite hash. Hold it until he clears the safety or gets even with him, then pass lead it up inside the hash.

reads.label: Why the Streak Holds Him
reads.text: The middle player on the trips side is on a streak, and that holds the middle defender so he cannot commit to the seam. The comeback on the short side holds the other one down. Now pass lead it in between the safety and the corner.

reads.label: Against Cover 2 With No Mid Read
reads.text: It works against Cover 2 too, but only when there is no middle defender: a Cover 2 sink, a Cover 2 blitz, or the user leaving the mid read. Split the two safeties with it.

reads.label: The Checkdowns
reads.text: Against match or man, or when the seam is taken away, there are three routes: the tight end in the flat, the shallow cross coming across, and the comeback on the short side as he breaks back toward the sideline.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Middle player on the trips side on a streak
plays.whenToUse: A Cover 3 beater and an excellent shot. One adjustment. The skinny seam goes inside of the middle safety, the streak and the comeback hold everybody else, and there are three checkdowns when it is not there.

plays.name: HB Swing

reads.label: No Pre-Snap Tell
reads.text: A lot of swings in this game come with an auto motion before the snap, and that is a tell. As soon as the user sees it, he comes to take it away. On this one everything happens after the snap.

reads.label: Four on Three
reads.text: Three blockers out there, so even if they bring three defenders it is a four on three. Everybody runs up the field and it just looks like pass routes. Drop it out to him with three blockers in front.

reads.label: On the Goal Line
reads.text: Really good inside the red zone. Most people play tight down there to take away the inside runs, the user does not know to fly out, and you walk it in behind three blockers.

reads.label: The Backside Slant
reads.text: The option route on the backside most of the time turns into a slant. If you do not like the look outside and everybody leaves the middle of the field, throw it.

reads.label: The QB Draw
reads.text: If they have four defenders out there and the option route runs a hitch instead, take off and turn it into a QB draw up the middle.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field, and give yourself room with the running back
plays.whenToUse: A swing with no pre-snap tell. Three blockers in front of the back makes it four on three even when they bring three, it is great on the goal line, and the backside slant and the QB draw are there when it is not.

plays.name: PA Deep Choice

reads.label: The Wheel Against Match
reads.text: The go to match beater in this scheme, against Quarters and Palms. The key is the switch release, the slot fade wheel with the post. The safety and the corner read one and two, and because both get vertical on the same plane, it is almost an impossible read for the safety to get over in time. Bomb it over the top.

reads.label: The Option Post Against Two High Match
reads.text: The option route we motioned in turns into a post against two high match, and he gets really nice separation as he breaks off the safety.

reads.label: The Short Side Post
reads.text: If the switch release happens earlier, the post from the short side can get open against match. Against Cover 3 the option route pulls the middle safety back, the slot fade pulls the corner out, and the post is wide open for twenty five yards.

reads.label: The Comeback
reads.text: Comebacks are actually pretty good against match. Throw it as he breaks.

reads.label: The Hole Shot Against Cover 2
reads.text: Against Cover 2, throw the slot fade wheel as a hole shot as he cuts up the sideline in behind the flat defender. Drop it in front of the safety.

reads.label: The Rub Against Man
reads.text: Not a man beater, but against man the post and the slot fade come together and make a natural rub. The slot fade is wide open, and the post breaks in with separation.

reads.label: The Back on the Option
reads.text: The checkdown. Against man he breaks inside or outside. Against zone he sits down.

adjustments: Running back to the wide side of the field
Motion the outside receiver on the wide side (the option route) in
The slot who becomes the outside receiver on the wide side on a comeback
Outside receiver on the short side on a post
Running back on an option route, or leave him on the play action block for time
plays.whenToUse: The go to way to beat match in this scheme, and it works against Cover 2 and Cover 3 as well. All four vertical routes are options against match. Get in practice mode and see all the ways these routes get open.

plays.name: Deep Choice

reads.label: The Deep Crosser
reads.text: A unique crosser that gets super deep down the field and is very hard to cover. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2, if the linebacker stays at about ten yards he gets to fifteen or twenty. Throw it early between the hashes, or later on the wide side once he clears.

reads.label: The Option Route
reads.text: The super wide splits and the option routes are the two things that make the veer and shoot unique. Against Cover 3 and single high he runs up the field and settles into a curl. Against two high, and especially match, he turns it into a dig that is very hard for the match defender to cover.

reads.label: The Dig Against Match
reads.text: This is match coverage, with the safety playing at depth, and it is really hard for him to drive on this option route. As he cuts across the field he is going to option into the dig. Third and 20, we throw that for 22 yards.

reads.label: The Backside Post
reads.text: Against Cover 2 the option route breaks inside, the crosser breaks deeper over the top, and they pull the linebackers inside, mid read included. Wait for the post and fire it over the top.

reads.label: The Checkdown
reads.text: Everybody is getting vertical. Pressure in your face, check it down to the running back on his option route.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver on the wide side on a post
Outside receiver on the short side on a streak
Running back on an option route
plays.whenToUse: The deep crosser, the option route and the post together make it a really good match play: the cross, the post vertical and the option route all give match trouble. Against zone the option sits, and the back is underneath.

plays.name: QB G Down

reads.label: Out of Empty
reads.text: A very good quarterback run. It is out of empty, so they are not expecting it, and the trips are away from the run side, so the defense lines up away from where we are going.

reads.label: The Blocking
reads.text: A down block from the tackle, the tight end goes to the linebacker, and the guard pulls around for the edge. We outnumber them five on four on the run side.

reads.label: Bounce It or Cut It
reads.text: Either bounce it to the outside and turn the corner, or cut it up into the hole the blocking opens with the receiver blocking out in front.

reads.label: On the Goal Line
reads.text: A very good goal line and red zone run. Pound it right through the hole and make the linebacker miss.

plays.whenToUse: The quarterback run out of empty. Trips away from the run side pull the defense the wrong way, the guard pulls for the edge, and it is five on four where the ball is going. It also punishes a defense that likes to stunt.

plays.name: Dagger

reads.label: The Deep Cross
reads.text: The first route. Read the flat defender on the short side: does he get depth underneath it, or stay shallow enough to let the cross get up over his head? He stops at about ten, put it at about twenty, the streak runs the defenders off.

reads.label: Against Match
reads.text: This setup works really well against match. The verticals and the drag pull guys out, and then the crosser gets up over the top.

reads.label: The Post Sit High Low
reads.text: If the deep cross is taken away and they are playing shallow on the drag, the post sit settles in the zone in the big pocket the seam ball left. Plenty of time.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: The drag and the cross become a high low on the linebackers. Against man, the tight end drag runs away from his man.

reads.label: The Seam Against Cover 2
reads.text: Most of the time the middle slot is the run off route, but against two high it is a Cover 2 beater. A tight throw, but it is there.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver on the wide side on a post sit
plays.whenToUse: The dagger concept out of empty: the deep cross over the flat defender first, the post sit and the drag as a high low underneath, and the seam against Cover 2.

plays.name: RPO Alert QB Counter

reads.label: Pick a Side
reads.text: The bubble is on the short side and the seam is on the wide side, so you can read either one. If there is no defender over the seam or nobody over the bubble pre-snap, read that side first.

reads.label: Read the Bubble
reads.text: If the defender over the bubble widens out with it at the snap, the bubble is taken away. Keep it.

reads.label: The QB Counter
reads.text: The guards come across and you step up ahead of the edge defender, get up the field with the blocking in front. As long as you can get around the edge, the blocking works so well.

reads.label: The Bubble One on One
reads.text: If the safety jumps inside at the snap, there is a one on one block outside. Throw that bubble right away.

reads.label: The Bubble Safety Valve
reads.text: If you start the counter and they are all coming, you can still flip it out to the bubble. It lets you get rid of the football instead of eating it.

reads.label: Read the Seam
reads.text: If you are reading the wide side, read the overhang. He bites down, widens out or goes inside, throw the seam. He stays on the seam, keep it with the quarterback.

adjustments: Bubble to the short side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The quarterback counter with a bubble on one side and a seam on the other. Pick whichever side you like better pre-snap and read that defender.

plays.name: Jet Touch Pass

reads.label: The Jet
reads.text: Bring him across and throw it to him. The running back leads, three blockers out front, and you get the perimeter and the ball in a playmaker's hands in the open field.

reads.label: One Motion, Three Plays
reads.text: Jet Power Read, Jet Touch Pass and Fake Jet FB Wheel all use this jet motion, so they play off each other. Start with this one, because the user sees the motion and starts to move, and that opens up the power read and the fake.

reads.label: On the Goal Line
reads.text: Really good in the red zone too. They crowd the box to take away the inside runs, and it is really hard to do that and have the speed to stay outside on the edge.

plays.whenToUse: The base call off the jet motion: bring him across, flip it, three blockers in front. Run it first, so the user starts chasing the motion.

plays.name: Fake Jet FB Wheel

reads.label: Set It Up First
reads.text: The third play off this jet motion. Run Jet Power Read and Jet Touch Pass first, because what we want is the motion coming across pulling the user and the linebackers down. No adjustments: just start with the two receiver side to the wide side of the field.

reads.label: The Curl
reads.text: The outside receiver runs a curl. If the flat defender jumps down, the curl sits down in the middle of the field where all the linebackers left to play the jet, and you drop it in.

reads.label: The Cross
reads.text: If they leave the middle of the field on the fake, the slot cross comes into the open area where the linebackers were.

reads.label: Underneath Early
reads.text: If you see everyone drop out, do not wait. Throw it early underneath as he cuts up the field, for nine yards on first and ten.

adjustments: Two receiver side to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The shot off the jet motion. The fake pulls the user and the linebackers down, the curl sits where they left, the cross comes in behind them, and there is an early throw underneath.

plays.name: PA Double Switch

reads.label: Four Verticals
reads.text: A streak on the inside, a wheel from the middle receiver and a post over the top: four vertical routes down the field with a checkdown to the back. The play action helps hold the linebackers down.

reads.label: The Post Behind the Streak
reads.text: The route thrown the most. The streak we motioned over pulls the safeties back, and the post breaks in behind it. Against Cover 2 he does not get deep enough in time, throw it right over the middle.

reads.label: The Streak Up the Seam
reads.text: If the safeties widen out too far, match or Cover 2 with no deep middle player, throw the streak we motioned over up the seam. Watch the user bite on the play action.

reads.label: The Wheel
reads.text: The streak and the post pull everybody back, and the wheel gets up in behind the flat defender. Drop it in.

reads.label: The Checkdown
reads.text: Pressure in your face and everyone underneath the vertical routes, check it down to the running back as he sits down.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field
Motion the slot receiver across and put him on a streak
plays.whenToUse: Four verticals off play action: the motioned streak pulls the safeties back, the post comes in behind him, the wheel gets behind the flat defender and the back is the checkdown.

plays.name: Double Smash Seam

reads.label: The Corner Against Zone
reads.text: Run it almost like flood. Look to the corner route on the wide side: the flat defender stays down, the streak runs the deep defender off, throw the corner up along the sideline.

reads.label: The Corners Against Man
reads.text: Matching corner routes on each side of the field. If it is man after the snap, throw either one. The side with no streak is the clearer throw, just one on one.

reads.label: The Back Against Match
reads.text: A concept built to beat match coverage. The vertical routes pull every match defender outside the hash, and the back gets a one on one with the linebacker up the middle. With a fast back on a linebacker, hit him over the top.

reads.label: Against Cover 2
reads.text: If the user is using the mid read and stays too shallow, or there is no middle read on the field, the back splits the safeties.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: Everything covered and pressure in your face, the drag comes across the field as the checkdown.

adjustments: Running back to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver on the wide side on a streak
Outside receiver on the short side on a drag
plays.whenToUse: A smash concept on both sides with the back up the seam. The corners beat zone and man, and the back on a linebacker is the answer to match, which is getting more popular every year.

plays.name: Switch Slot Cross

reads.label: The Corner Route
reads.text: One of our two best man beaters, with Ins Slot Corner. Look to the corner route first. Good separation as he breaks, let it fly.

reads.label: The Natural Rub
reads.text: The Z post on the wide side creates a natural rub, and the corner comes open behind it.

reads.label: The Z Post
reads.text: No safety in the middle of the field, hit the Z post. A post safety, throw it as he breaks in, and the rub helps him too.

reads.label: Three Levels in the Middle
reads.text: The shallow cross, the dig coming in behind it and the running back. Hit the shallow with separation, the dig over the top, or the back breaking underneath.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field
Wheel route on the wide side on a corner route
Optional: block the running back if you think they are bringing pressure
plays.whenToUse: The second go to man beater next to Ins Slot Corner. The corner route behind the natural rub, the Z post, and three levels in the middle of the field.

plays.name: RPO Alert Bubble

reads.label: Count the Bubble Side
reads.text: Trips to the wide side, and read the defender over the top of the bubble. Two defenders over three, throw it.

reads.label: Two High: Run It
reads.text: The veer and shoot is not just a pass offense. Two safeties back and only five in the box, we have five linemen and the back. Six on five, run it right at them.

reads.label: He Bites Down: Throw It
reads.text: The overhang bites down on the run, throw the bubble. Three on three outside, everybody gets pinned inside and you are gone up the sideline.

reads.label: Make Them Respect the Splits
reads.text: If they are loading the box and not respecting the wide splits, throw the bubble every single time. They will change their formation, or you get ten and twenty yard plays all day.

reads.label: The Backside Option
reads.text: The solo receiver on the short side is on an option route. Mostly a hitch against zone, and if it is man and the linebackers all bite down, the skinny post.

reads.label: On the Goal Line
reads.text: A really good goal line and red zone play. They load the box to take away the middle and nobody lines up over the bubble. Throw it every time.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The bubble RPO for two high looks and for people who do not respect the perimeter. Run it against two high, throw it when they will not line up with your splits.
